subject: Tenant mapping discrepancy and settlement split — need invoice pairing
messages:
From: Sam Green <sam.green@brightlayer.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: AWS Marketplace <aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected split on June marketplace invoice (BrightLayer / Redwood)

Hi Naomi —

Hope you’re well. We received Redwood’s June marketplace invoice yesterday but the settlement lines don’t match our internal tenant mapping. Specifically: a large portion of usage that should be attributed to our EU tenant (org_id: BL-EU-01) was billed under the US entity, and the VAT classification on the invoice shows 0% for those rows. This is blocking our AP team from releasing payment.

Key details:
- BrightLayer invoice reference: BL-INV-6721 (your document attached)
- Amount on hold at our end: $42,180.00
- Affected seats: prod-analytics and prod-export pipelines (tenant ids included in attached CSV)

Can you confirm whether this is a marketplace metering/tenant-routing issue on Redwood’s listing or an upstream aggregation problem from AWS? We need: an interim ledger pairing so we can clear the payment and any VAT evidence for the EU tenant.

Thanks — I’ve attached the tenant list and our reconciliation snapshot.

Regards,
Sam Green
Finance Lead, BrightLayer Inc.
[attachment: tenant_list_brightlayer_202706.csv (csv, 18KB)]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Green <sam.green@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected split on June marketplace invoice (BrightLayer / Redwood)

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the clear note and the CSV — I’ve looped in Karthik and Marcus to help trace the mapping. We also pulled the marketplace invoice that hit our payout ledger (attached).

Immediate next steps:
1) Marcus — can you pull the marketplace metering export for the BrightLayer listing between 2027-06-01 and 2027-06-30 and compare the tenant label fields against Sam’s CSV?
2) Karthik — if this is a routing/tag mismatch (tenant labels getting dropped during marketplace aggregation), we should open a support ticket with AWS and request a corrected invoice or a debit memo.
3) Sam — if BrightLayer can provide the EU VAT registration number for BL-EU-01 and the AP contact for remittance once we provide an interim pairing, that will speed approval.

I’ve attached the invoice I see in our ledger for reference.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
[attachment: marketplace_invoice_202706.pdf (pdf, 76KB)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Sam Green <sam.green@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected split on June marketplace invoice (BrightLayer / Redwood)

On Wed, Jun 30, 2027 at 10:32 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sam —
> 
> Thanks for the clear note and the CSV — I’ve looped in Karthik and Marcus to help trace the mapping. We also pulled the marketplace invoice that hit our payout ledger (attached).
> 
> Immediate next steps:
> 1) Marcus — can you pull the marketplace metering export for the BrightLayer listing between 2027-06-01 and 2027-06-30 and compare the tenant label fields against Sam’s CSV?

Thanks — I pulled the metering export and did an initial pass. Findings so far:
- The usage rows in question do include a "tenant_label" value from the instrumented SDK, but the marketplace aggregation layer appears to have collapsed tenant_label to the seller_entity_id in several rollup buckets.
- The rows aggregated under seller_entity_id RED-NA-01 contain mixed tenant_label values: BL-US-02 and BL-EU-01. The invoice lines we received had the seller entity only, so the downstream invoice didn’t preserve tenant-level granularity.

I attached a small snapshot (usage_snapshot_2027-06.csv) showing sample rows and the aggregation keys.

Recommendation:
- We should ask AWS Marketplace to issue either (A) a split invoice that attributes BL-EU-01 consumption separately with VAT, or (B) a debit/credit memo pair so BrightLayer’s AP can net the EU VAT correctly.
- Meanwhile, we can provide BrightLayer with a temporary ledger pairing file (our internal breakout by tenant) so they can unblock payment. This will not change the marketplace invoice but will provide traceability.

I’ll open a support ticket with AWS this morning (including the snapshot and a request for corrected tax treatment). Karthik — can you own the external asks and escalate if the ticket response is slow?

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
[attachment: usage_snapshot_2027-06.csv (csv, 124KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sam Green <sam.green@brightlayer.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected split on June marketplace invoice (BrightLayer / Redwood)

Thanks Marcus — I’ve just opened AWS case #1234567890 with the following request: 
- Provide per-tenant breakout for RED-NA-01 for invoice BL-INV-6721
- Re-issue invoice with separate EU lines or provide debit memo referencing VAT chargeable lines
- Confirm whether the seller_entity_id rollup can be disabled for BrightLayer’s listing going forward (they want tenant-level granularity)

Sam — for the interim pairing, attached is a proposed tenant-mapping.xlsx that maps the marketplace aggregation buckets to BrightLayer’s tenant ids and shows the VAT basis. If you confirm BL-EU-01’s VAT registration (VAT: EU12345678) and approve the pairing, our finance team will email a ledger-pairing statement BrightLayer can attach to its AP ticket.

If AWS confirms they can’t re-issue before your payment cutoff, we will commit to providing a signed ledger reconciliation note from Redwood that BrightLayer can use for one-off settlement; we will reconcile in our July settlement cycle.

Next steps: Sam to confirm VAT number and whether BrightLayer accepts a temporary ledger pairing for AP. Marcus and I to track AWS case and escalate to AWS account team if no response in 48 hours.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[attachment: tenant-mapping-proposal.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)]

From: Sam Green <sam.green@brightlayer.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2027 16:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected split on June marketplace invoice (BrightLayer / Redwood)

Hi team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and for opening the AWS ticket. Confirming: BL-EU-01 VAT registration is EU12345678 (attached VAT cert). BrightLayer is willing to accept Redwood’s ledger pairing note as interim evidence so AP will release the payment by EOD Monday (2027-07-05) provided we get the signed pairing PDF.

Please send the ledger pairing statement to accounts@brightlayer.com and cc my AP lead (ap@brightlayer.com). Also copy in your payments contact so we can reconcile when AWS issues any corrected invoices or debit memos.

Appreciate the help — Sam

[attachment: brightlayer_vat_cert_BL-EU-01.pdf (pdf, 22KB)]
